newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi SABIC net falls to 4.41 bln riyals.
newsitem.headline: Saudi SABIC net falls to 4.41 bln riyals.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) on Monday blamed lower petrochemical prices in world markets for a 29.8 decrease in its 1996 net profit.
SABIC, 70 percent owned by the Saudi government, said in a statement it made a 4.41 billion riyal ($1.176 billion) net profit in 1996, sharply down from 6.28 billion riyals in 1995.

Saudi Arabia's Industry and Electricity Minister Hashem bin Abdullah bin Hashem Yamani attributed the fall in net profit to lower petrochemical prices, "despite a four percent increase in production and marketing in 1996".

"SABIC's earnings were especially affected by the fall in prices of polyethylene, methanol, styrene, ehtylene glycol and polyvinyl chloride," Yamani, who is also chairman of SABIC, said in the company statement.

Yamani said SABIC's total production in 1996 increased four percent from a year ago to 23 million tonnes of various products. He said SABIC marketed 17 million tonnes, but gave no comparative figures.
"SABIC's products have directly resulted in the expansion and diversification of the national downstream industries and the development of the Saudi agriculture sector," Yamani said.

Vice-chairman Ibrahim bin Salameh said SABIC produced more than 12.3 million tonnes of chemicals, two million tonnes of plastics, about 2.8 million tonnes of steel and iron, more than four million tonnes of fertilisers and 1.2 million tonnes of other products in 1996.
SABIC said its board of directors proposed a 2.5 billion riyal cash dividend to shareholders for 1996, down from three billion riyals for 1995.

SABIC accounts for around five percent of the world's petrochemical production. It has embarked on an ambitious programme to raise its annual production capacity to 28 million tonnes by the year 2000 from the current 23 million tonnes.
